Fort Worth Truck Accident Lawyer (2025): What to Do After a Crash with a Big Rig in Texas

You’re driving down I-35, minding your own business, when an 18-wheeler starts drifting into your lane. You honk, you brake—but there’s nowhere to go. The impact is loud, sudden, and terrifying.

In a split second, your life changes.

Truck accidents in Fort Worth aren’t just “big car wrecks.” They’re catastrophic events involving powerful commercial vehicles, complex insurance systems, and serious injuries that can take months or years to recover from.

If this sounds familiar, you need to know your rights—and you need a Fort Worth truck accident lawyer who knows how to fight the trucking companies and get you full compensation.

That’s where The Lange Firm comes in.

Why Truck Accidents Are Different from Car Accidents

Truck accident cases are more complicated than regular car wrecks for one simple reason: there’s a lot more at stake.

A fully loaded tractor-trailer can weigh 80,000 pounds. When it collides with a 3,000-pound car, the results are devastating. Victims often face:

  • Severe injuries (spinal cord, brain, or internal trauma)

  • Long-term disability or loss of income

  • Emotional trauma and PTSD

  • Sky-high medical bills

And that’s just the beginning. Unlike ordinary drivers, truckers are often backed by large corporations and aggressive insurance carriers. Their job is to minimize your payout—or deny it altogether.

The Lange Firm knows these tactics inside and out and fights to make sure victims get every dollar they deserve.

Common Causes of Truck Accidents in Fort Worth

Fort Worth sits at the crossroads of major Texas highways—like I-35W, I-20, and U.S. 287—making it a hotspot for commercial truck traffic. With that comes higher risk.

Common causes of truck crashes in the area include:

  • Driver fatigue: Long hours behind the wheel cause slow reaction times and drowsiness.

  • Speeding and reckless driving: Truckers rushing to meet delivery deadlines often drive dangerously.

  • Distracted driving: Phones, GPS devices, and paperwork can all take attention off the road.

  • Improper maintenance: Worn brakes, bald tires, or faulty steering can cause deadly accidents.

  • Overloaded or unbalanced cargo: Too much weight or uneven loads make trucks harder to control.

  • Alcohol or drug use: Even prescription drugs can impair reaction times.

Whatever the cause, victims deserve accountability—and The Lange Firm knows how to uncover it.

Who Can Be Held Liable in a Truck Accident

One of the biggest challenges in a truck accident case is figuring out who’s actually responsible. Unlike a car crash, it’s rarely just one person.

Potentially liable parties may include:

  • The truck driver (for negligence or rule violations)

  • The trucking company (for unsafe schedules or poor training)

  • The cargo company (for improper loading)

  • The maintenance provider (for faulty repairs)

  • The truck manufacturer (for defective parts)

These companies often point fingers at each other to avoid paying. That’s why you need a Fort Worth truck accident lawyer who can investigate every angle—and hold the right people accountable.

Types of Compensation Available After a Truck Accident

When you’re injured in a truck accident, your losses go far beyond the medical bills sitting on your kitchen counter. Texas law allows victims to recover economic and non-economic damages, including:

  • Medical expenses (current and future)

  • Lost wages and loss of earning capacity

  • Vehicle repair or replacement costs

  • Pain and suffering

  • Mental anguish and emotional distress

  • Loss of companionship or enjoyment of life

In some cases, you may even qualify for punitive damages—extra compensation designed to punish especially reckless behavior (like drunk or drowsy driving).

The Lange Firm carefully calculates every category of damages so that clients get the full financial recovery they deserve.

Steps to Take After a Truck Accident in Fort Worth

Truck accidents can leave victims shaken and confused. Here’s what to do immediately after the crash to protect your health—and your legal rights:

1. Call 911. Get medical help for yourself and others. Police reports are crucial evidence later.

2. Seek medical attention. Even if you feel okay, adrenaline can hide serious injuries.

3. Take photos and videos. Capture the vehicles, license plates, road conditions, and visible injuries.

4. Get witness information. Names, phone numbers, and statements can support your case.

5. Don’t speak to insurance adjusters. They may call quickly, but their goal is to pay as little as possible.

6. Contact a lawyer. The earlier The Lange Firm is involved, the better your chances of protecting evidence and building a strong case.

Why Evidence Disappears Quickly in Truck Accident Cases

One of the biggest mistakes victims make is waiting too long to call a lawyer. Trucking companies often send investigators to the scene within hours of a crash—and crucial evidence can vanish fast.

Key evidence includes:

  • Driver logs and rest schedules

  • Black box data (showing speed, braking, and steering)

  • GPS and dispatch records

  • Maintenance and inspection logs

  • Drug and alcohol test results

  • Cargo loading documentation

If you wait too long, that evidence may be “lost” or destroyed. The Lange Firm acts quickly to preserve it through formal legal action—making sure nothing disappears that could help your claim.

Federal Regulations That Affect Trucking Cases

Truck drivers and their employers must follow strict federal safety regulations set by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA).

These rules cover:

  • Hours of service (to prevent fatigue)

  • Weight limits

  • Maintenance schedules

  • Drug and alcohol testing

  • Driver qualifications and background checks

When companies cut corners, people get hurt. Violations of these federal rules often form the foundation of a strong negligence case.

Common Truck Accident Injuries

Because of the sheer size and force of trucks, injuries are often catastrophic. Victims may suffer:

  • Traumatic brain injuries (TBI)

  • Spinal cord damage or paralysis

  • Broken bones and fractures

  • Internal bleeding or organ damage

  • Severe burns or lacerations

  • Permanent disfigurement

Recovery can take years—and medical costs can climb into the hundreds of thousands. That’s why having a lawyer who understands long-term damages is essential.

The Lange Firm works closely with medical experts to project future costs so that clients aren’t left paying out of pocket later.

Wrongful Death in Truck Accident Cases

When a loved one is killed in a truck crash, the emotional and financial toll is overwhelming.

Under Texas law, the surviving spouse, children, or parents may file a wrongful death claim to seek compensation for:

  • Funeral and burial costs

  • Lost income and financial support

  • Emotional suffering and mental anguish

  • Loss of companionship and guidance

The Lange Firm handles these cases with compassion and determination, fighting to bring families the justice they deserve.

How Much Does a Truck Accident Lawyer Cost?

Here’s one less thing to stress about: when you hire The Lange Firm, you don’t pay anything upfront.

The firm works on a contingency fee basis, meaning they only get paid if you win. Their payment comes out of your settlement—not your pocket.

That structure ensures your lawyer is fully invested in your success and motivated to fight for the highest possible recovery.

Why Hire a Local Fort Worth Truck Accident Lawyer

Fort Worth might be part of a major metro area, but every county courthouse—and every judge—has its own rhythm.

A local lawyer who understands Tarrant County courts, Texas juries, and local insurance adjusters gives you an advantage.

The Lange Firm combines local insight with statewide experience, representing clients across Texas in serious truck and auto accident cases. Whether your crash happened on I-20, Loop 820, or Highway 287, the firm knows how to navigate the system and win.

How Long You Have to File a Truck Accident Claim in Texas

The clock starts ticking the moment the crash happens.

Texas law gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. Miss that deadline, and you could lose your right to compensation forever.

That’s why it’s critical to speak with a Fort Worth truck accident lawyer as soon as possible. Even if you’re still in recovery, your attorney can start preserving evidence and protecting your case.

The Lange Firm’s Approach to Truck Accident Cases

Every trucking case is unique—but The Lange Firm’s approach stays consistent:

  • Investigate quickly to preserve evidence.

  • Handle insurance companies so you don’t have to.

  • Calculate full damages (including future losses).

  • Negotiate aggressively for maximum settlement.

  • Go to trial if necessary—and win.

Unlike firms that treat clients like case numbers, The Lange Firm offers personal attention and honest advice. You’ll work directly with attorney Evan Lange, not a rotating team of assistants.

That’s how trust is built—and how results are achieved.

What to Expect When You Work with The Lange Firm

When you contact The Lange Firm, you’ll start with a free consultation where you can share your story, ask questions, and understand your options.

From there, the firm handles everything: evidence gathering, insurance negotiations, medical documentation, and, if needed, trial preparation.

You focus on healing. The firm focuses on winning.

Take the First Step Toward Justice

Truck accidents can leave deep scars—physical, emotional, and financial. But you don’t have to face the aftermath alone.

If you or someone you love was injured in a truck accident near Fort Worth, reach out to The Lange Firm’s Fort Worth truck accident lawyer today.

You’ll get clear answers, compassionate support, and a legal team that fights for results—not excuses.

You’ve already survived the crash. Now it’s time to rebuild—with the right team on your side.
